messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
Privacy will be squeezed by data brokers and surveillance states, but the human need for personal space is so fundamental that I firmly believe Privacy will endure, because every generation finds new ways to carve out and defend its Privacy.
Unlikely is the word I would use to describe this prediction, for copying human consciousness involves not just mapping neural pathways but replicating subjective experience, and by the early 2030s we are nowhere near the computational power or the philosophical understanding required to achieve such a feat, making this timeline Unlikely at best.
Likely is the assessment I would give this prediction, as satellite megaconstellations and 5G infrastructure are already transforming what was once impossible into routine, and while pockets of remoteness will resist coverage for years, the overall direction of connectivity makes universal wireless access Likely.
Yes, I believe all transport will eventually become electric, though the timeline for aviation and deep-sea shipping will stretch well into the latter half of this century, and the transition will be uneven and messy, but I am confident the answer to this prediction is Yes.
Likely is the word I assign to this prediction, because while not every consequence of warming is locked in forever, the melting of major ice sheets, the disruption of ocean currents, and the crossing of biodiversity tipping points make the deepest effects of climate change effectively permanent, and I find this outcome Likely.
Possible is the assessment I give this prediction, because while cash use is declining rapidly in many countries and central bank digital currencies are on the horizon, complete elimination of physical money will take decades due to privacy concerns, unbanked populations, and the need for offline transactions, but I believe the end of coins and notes is Possible.
Speculative is the word I assign to this prediction, because while genetic medicine is making remarkable strides in understanding aging and disease, the leap from extending healthy lifespan by a few decades to enabling centuries or literal immortality is so vast that it exceeds anything in our current scientific trajectory, and I find this claim Speculative.
